title: Console color anchoring and chart-legend contrast update for thematic brand variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Brand-theme variants are currently applied by swapping a small set of surface colors, which causes inconsistent perceived color relationships in charts and legend items and frequently fails contrast targets in dark mode for low-saturation brand palettes. Goal: Introduce a color-anchoring strategy that maps brand hues to semantic token anchors (primary/secondary/interactive) and applies deterministic contrast-preserving transforms for chart legends, table row accents, and button outlines. This ticket covers the design work: token mapping rules, component overrides for charts/tables/legend items, Figma token libraries, and accessibility validation criteria. The outcome should be a token bridge and component override spec that Eng can implement and QA can validate across a matrix of 12 brand variants in light and dark modes.
acceptance_criteria: Token mapping spec published: algorithm + examples for mapping brand hue to semantic tokens (primary, accent, muted, emphasis) for light and dark
Chart legend items maintain minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for label text against background in both modes or use outlined swatches where necessary
Button and link affordances preserve target contrast ratios (text >= 4.5:1, icons >= 3:1 depending on size) across 12 sample brand palettes
Figma components updated and handed off with tokens file v2 and usage notes
Design sign-off from PM and Accessibility engineer documented in comments
Implementation hooks defined: token names, expected runtime transforms, and a fallback mapping for low-saturation brands
design_notes: We will anchor brand colors to semantic tokens rather than directly swapping component colors. Anchoring rules: map brand hue to --color-accent-hue, then generate semantic tokens with predefined lightness adjustments (+/- delta) and contrast clamps. For dark mode, invert the lightness delta and apply saturation boosting for brand swatches in small legend squares. For charts: prefer stroked legend swatches when fill contrast is insufficient; add a 1px neutral outline token for small swatches. For tables: use subtle left-border accent token derived from accent-hue with 18% opacity in light, 30% in dark. Provide CSS custom-property examples and a JSON token snippet for runtime teams. Include guidance for designers: when a brand falls below saturation threshold, use the provided fallbackAccent token (derived from brand but nudged toward neutral) to maintain readability.
decisions: Use semantic token anchors instead of direct brand token swaps to keep component geometry’s perceived color relationships intact
Adopt contrast-preserving transforms rather than fixed brand color overrides to support a large set of brand variants
For small legend swatches (<18px), prefer stroked outline + fill combo to meet contrast requirements
Expose a single runtime toggle 'brand-mode: permissive|strict' for teams that want faithful brand color vs teams that prioritize accessibility

qa_notes: QA should run the color matrix test harness against 12 brand palettes (listed in Confluence) in both light and dark. Record screenshots and file any visual regressions as ENG tickets.
handoff_instructions: Attach token JSON v2, Figma library link, example CSS custom properties, and a small runnable demo (Storybook) that toggles brand-mode. Provide Eng with list of explicit token names to implement: --color-accent-hue, --color-accent-500, --color-accent-300, --chart-legend-outline, --table-row-accent, --fallback-accent. Include the saturation threshold parameter and examples for fallback mapping.
